“The HBT puzzle is solved by including strong pionic final state interactions, and the RHIC Hbt puzzle and the chiral symmetry restoration phase transition are related by the same pion optical potential.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of pion emission from the hot, dense matter produced in relativistic heavy-ion collisions.
the dynamics of pion emission from the quark-gluon plasma.
the dynamics of pion emission and HBT correlations in relativistic heavy ion collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have a model for the emission of pion pairs from the fireball which reproduces the STAR HBT data and the resonance-coupled pion spectrum, and that the model is consistent with the chiral phase-transition picture.
the DWEF model provides an excellent fit to all of the STAR data, with the only input being a formation temperature and a chemical potential.
our model is able to reproduce the STAR data with a single set of parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HBT puzzle is solved by a chiral phase transition in the early stages of heavy-ion collisions at RHIC.
the HBT puzzle can be solved in the context of a chiral phase transition and that the RHIC Hbt puzzle and the chiral transition are intimately connected.

the RHIC pion data can be understood as the result of a pion source that is very hot and dense, and that the pionic distorted wave emission function model ( DWEF ) is a very useful tool for studying the properties of the source.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pionic final state interactions are very important for the description of the HBT puzzle and the pionic spectrum.
the HBT puzzle, the apparent failure of the hydrodynamic model to account for HBT data, may be resolved by the inclusion of final-state interactions.
a simple, phenomenological, relativistic distorted wave formalism, when applied to the RHIC data, leads to a pion emission function that has strong attractive and absorptive effects.
